Theme

# Philosophy quotes about courage

Courage is the virtue of facing fear without abandoning judgment—central to ethics from Aristotle to modern existential resolve.

14 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophers ask whether courage is fearlessness or right action amid fear, and how it relates to recklessness, endurance, and moral courage in public life.

## In the history of philosophy

Greek andreia, Confucian and martial ethics, Stoic endurance, and civil-disobedience traditions all refine the concept.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Ralph Waldo Emerson](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ralph-waldo-emerson) , [Bertrand Russell](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/bertrand-russell) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius) , [Paul Tillich](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/paul-tillich) , [Søren Kierkegaard](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/soren-kierkegaard)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is courage in philosophy?

Typically a mean between cowardice and rashness: persevering for worthy ends despite fear.

### Is moral courage different from physical courage?

Many ethicists distinguish facing bodily danger from risking status, career, or approval for a principle.
